card.title: Viśvāmitra
card.sub: From king to seer · the story behind the Gāyatrī mantra

lines.text: Long ago, there lived a mighty king named Kauśika.
lines.tts: Long ago, there lived a mighty king, named Kaushika.

lines.text: One day, hunting with his army, he came to the forest hermitage of the sage Vasiṣṭha.
lines.tts: One day, hunting with his army, he came to the forest hermitage of the sage, Vasishtha.

lines.text: The sage welcomed them all, and through his sacred cow Nandinī, he fed the entire army.
lines.tts: The sage welcomed them all. And through his sacred cow, Nandini, he fed the entire army.

lines.text: The king wanted the wondrous cow for himself. When Vasiṣṭha refused, he tried to take her by force.
lines.tts: The king wanted the wondrous cow for himself. When Vasishtha refused, he tried to take her by force.

lines.text: But every arrow, every weapon, fell silent before the sage's staff.
lines.tts: But every arrow, every weapon, fell silent before the sage's staff.

lines.text: Kauśika understood. The power of a sage was greater than the power of any king.
lines.tts: Kaushika understood. The power of a sage, was greater than the power of any king.

lines.text: So he laid down his crown, and went into the forest to become a sage himself.
lines.tts: So he laid down his crown, and went into the forest, to become a sage himself.

lines.text: For years he meditated. Pride, desire and anger tested him. Again and again, he fell.
lines.tts: For years, he meditated. Pride, desire, and anger, tested him. Again and again, he fell.

lines.text: And each time, he began again.
lines.tts: And each time, he began again.

lines.text: At last his mind became as still and clear as the dawn. Even Vasiṣṭha bowed to him, and called him Brahmarṣi, a great seer.
lines.tts: At last, his mind became as still and clear as the dawn. Even Vasishtha bowed to him, and called him, Brahmarishi. A great seer.

lines.text: In that stillness, Viśvāmitra saw a prayer of light. Not for power, but for an awakened mind.
lines.tts: In that stillness, Vishwamitra saw a prayer of light. Not for power, but for an awakened mind.
